## Direct competitors

These vendors sell AI credit analysis or memo drafting to UK SME lenders. None is a LinkedIn-visible individual engineer, which is the thing the bet offers.

| name | what | price | link |
|---|---|---|---|
| Crediflow AI (Manchester) | Automates financial spreading, bank-statement analysis and credit memos for commercial lenders. Raised £1.5m (2026 seed). | No public price. GetApp shows "No pricing info". | https://www.capterra.co.uk/software/1099158/Crediflow-AI |
| Arya.ai Cred AI | AI underwriting and credit memo automation. UK case study with MaxCap claims 10x underwriting productivity (vendor claim). | No public price found | https://arya.ai/success-stories/uk-lender-maxcap-increases-underwriting-productivity-with-cred-ai |
| Wiserfunding (London) | SME credit analytics and risk scoring. Partnered with FullCircl. | No public price found | https://www.fullcircl.com/using-fullcircl/fullcircl-wiserfunding-partnership-overview |
| Funding Xchange | Cloud underwriting platform. Automates decisions under £100k and semi-automates larger requests. | No public price found | https://www.openbanking.org.uk/regulated-providers/funding-xchange/ |
| Digilytics RevEL | AI document processing for SME fund approvals. | No public price found | https://ibsintelligence.com/ibsi-news/5-fintechs-leveraging-ai-to-reinvent-sme-lending-in-the-uk |
| nCino (incl. Numerated) | Full banking and lending platform with SME lending and spreading. | Custom quote only | https://www.capterra.com/p/140944/nCino/reviews/ |
| OakNorth, Parsewise, Ocrolus | AI credit intelligence, cross-document checks and statement analysis. Named in a 2026 vendor comparison. | No price in that source | https://llms.parsewise.ai/comparisons/compliance/parsewise-vs-ocrolus-vs-oaknorth-vs-numerated-sme-credit/ |

## Indirect and substitutes

- **Doing nothing:** analysts write memos by hand. This is the main substitute. I found no source that sizes it.
- **Existing agencies and vendors:** the bet says lenders hire from firms they already know. I have no source for this beyond the bet's own claim.
- **In-house builds:** Kriya describes building AI into its own credit workflow. https://www.kriya.co/blog/how-were-building-ai-into-how-kriya-works
- **Broker or lender platforms with their own tech:** Spark Finance publishes lender-facing technology and content. https://sparkfinance.co.uk/technology/lender-solutions
- **Other freelance AI engineers:** UK contractors compete on day rate (see Prices). I found no lending-specialist freelancer building in public.

## Prices

Quoted as found. Dates are those of the pages, not verified.

- Crediflow AI: no public price. GetApp lists "No pricing info". https://www.getapp.com/all-software/a/crediflow-ai/
- nCino: no official price sheet. Custom quotes. Reviewers cite high implementation and licence costs for smaller institutions. https://www.rfp.wiki/vendors/ncino
- LendingWise (a comparable loan-origination tool, not an AI memo vendor): $149 per user per month, listed on GetApp. https://www.getapp.com/all-software/a/crediflow-ai/
- Freelance benchmark, UK AI Engineer contracts (ITJobsWatch, six months to 1 May 2025): median £575/day, 90th percentile £875/day. https://www.itjobswatch.co.uk/contracts/uk/artificial%20intelligence%20engineer.do
- Freelance benchmark, Agentic AI Engineer, London (six months to 26 June 2026): median £600/day. https://www.itjobswatch.co.uk/contracts/london/agentic%20artificial%20intelligence%20engineer.do?p=6
- No lending-specific contractor rate found.

## What their customers complain about

There are no lender-voice reviews of AI memo tools in these sources. The complaints below are about neighbouring products, paraphrased from review aggregators. I have no one-line customer quotes.

- High upfront implementation cost and ongoing licence fees, especially for smaller institutions (nCino reviewers). https://www.rfp.wiki/vendors/ncino
- Long, resource-heavy implementations that need strong programme and change management (nCino reviewers). https://www.rfp.wiki/vendors/ncino
- Opaque pricing; total cost depends on Salesforce licences, services and core integrations. https://www.capterra.com/p/140944/nCino/reviews/
- Explainability and audit trail are treated as core requirements by regulators and law firms. This is commentary, not customer complaint, so it does not confirm the bet's "can't trace the figures" assumption (D1). https://finreglab.org/ai-machine-learning/explainability-and-fairness-of-machine-learning-in-credit-underwriting
- Agentic AI spreads AI-influenced actions across the credit file, which makes auditing harder (vendor-authored). https://lendfoundry.com/blog/ai-risk-management-for-lenders-what-regulators-are-watching-in-2026/

## Not found

- Any page I could open. WebFetch failed, so all facts are from search snippets and no page dates were checked.
- Published pricing for Crediflow, Arya, Wiserfunding, Funding Xchange, Digilytics, Numerated, Ocrolus and OakNorth.
- Reviews or forum threads from UK heads of credit about AI memo tools.
- Any lender saying in their own words that they distrust AI underwriting because they can't trace the figures. This is the bet's ASSUMPTION and stays unevidenced.
- G2 or Capterra reviews for Crediflow AI.
- Any lending-specialist freelancer building in public on LinkedIn, and any data on whether UK SME lenders buy from individual freelancers (D6).
- Contractor day rates specific to credit or lending.
- Moody's CreditLens, Zest and Cloverleaf. My search returned nothing on them. I did not look for live pages.
- Any UK SME lender's supplier due-diligence requirements for individuals.

summary_md:
- Crowded: at least 7 funded vendors sell AI credit analysis to UK SME lenders, but I found no individual engineer building in public in this niche.
- Price band: vendors publish no prices (quote only); freelance AI engineers run about £575–£875/day (ITJobsWatch).
- Loudest complaint: cost and long implementation for smaller lenders (nCino reviewers); no lender says they distrust AI because they can't trace figures, so that assumption is untested.
- Gap: vendors are opaque and enterprise-priced, so a visible builder with traceable figures is differentiated, but I found no evidence lenders buy from individuals (D6).
- Freshness: snippets only, no page opened, dates unchecked; some pages appear to be from 2025 to mid-2026.
questions: Which segment first: specialist SME lenders, brokers, or fintech CTOs? The competitor set differs for each.
Is the geography UK only, or UK plus EU/US lenders who might also follow you?
Can I retry with fetch access so I can open the pages and check dates and pricing, or should this stay at snippet level?
